label: Essay
summary: A reflective, argumentative essay that develops a stated opinion or lens on life into a full position piece.

slots.label: The Position
slots.description: The thesis in the author's own words — the stated opinion or lens on life the essay develops.

slots.label: Evidence Scenes
slots.description: Concrete lived moments that ground the argument — one scene is worth three paragraphs of theory.

slots.label: Counter-Tension
slots.description: The strongest opposing view or internal doubt, steelmanned honestly rather than dismissed.

slots.label: Earned Resolution
slots.description: Where the argument lands — what this lens changes about how to see, grown out of the evidence rather than asserted.

research.basis: Slots operationalize Gornick's situation-vs-story distinction — the thesis is 'the thing one has come to say,' evidence scenes are the situation that must be made to speak — and steelmanning research showing that engaging the strongest opposing view increases perceived credibility more than an undefended assertion.
citations: Gornick 2001, The Situation and the Story — separates the situation (circumstance, plot) from the story (the insight the writer has come to say); the personal essay's persona is 'the instrument of illumination'
Mill, On Liberty (via contemporary rhetoric/argumentation research) — steelmanning the opposing view before answering it signals intellectual honesty and increases argument credibility
McAdams & McLean 2013 — redemption sequences (bad-to-good arcs) track with well-being and read as more earned than asserted conclusions

ai_context: Distinguish situation from story in evidence_scenes: a scene that's situation-rich but hasn't yet said what it means needs the 'what does this say about the position' pass before it can serve as evidence.
If the position emerged through a hardship or reversal, naming that arc in earned_resolution (what grew out of it) makes the insight read as earned rather than stated.
